cards.statement: Azure DNS automatically delegates a purchased domain when an administrator creates its matching public zone.
cards.explanation: The domain owner updates the registrar's name-server delegation to the servers assigned to the Azure DNS zone. Creating the zone leaves this registrar task for the owner.
cards.misconception: Creating a public Azure DNS zone also updates the domain registrar's delegation.

source.title: Tutorial: Host your domain in Azure DNS

cards.statement: Azure Private DNS can autoregister a VM's secondary network interface in a linked private DNS zone.
cards.explanation: Azure Private DNS creates automatic VM records for the primary network interface. An administrator creates records manually for a VM's additional network interfaces.
cards.misconception: Autoregistration discovers and registers a VM's secondary network interfaces.

source.title: What is the autoregistration feature in Azure DNS private zones?

cards.statement: A VM using Azure-provided DNS can resolve records in a linked private zone with autoregistration disabled.
cards.explanation: A resolution link makes a private zone's existing records available to Azure-provided DNS clients in the linked network. Enabling VM record registration is a separate choice.

source.title: What is a virtual network link?

cards.statement: Azure DNS automatically empties an alias record set when an administrator deletes its Standard public IP target.
cards.explanation: Deleting an alias record's Standard public IP target leaves an empty record set in Azure DNS. This clears the dangling reference while retaining the record-set resource.

source.title: Azure DNS alias records overview

cards.statement: By default, VMs using custom DNS servers bypass those servers to query a linked Azure private DNS zone.
cards.explanation: VM queries go to their configured custom DNS servers first. The administrator configures those servers to forward the Azure private namespace to a resolver that can reach the linked zone.
cards.misconception: A linked Azure private DNS zone makes a VM bypass its configured custom DNS servers.

source.title: Troubleshoot DNS resolution failures caused by conditional forwarder misconfiguration in Azure

cards.statement: A regional Standard Load Balancer requires its backend VMs to belong to the same virtual network.
cards.explanation: A Standard Load Balancer's VM backend pool stays within a single virtual network. Its backend VMs may occupy different subnets in that network.

source.title: Azure Load Balancer SKUs

cards.statement: An administrator can permit IPv4 Load Balancer probes with an NSG rule using AzureLoadBalancer as its source.
cards.explanation: AzureLoadBalancer matches the source of IPv4 health probes. Configure an inbound NSG allow rule with that source and the probe's destination port.

source.title: Azure Load Balancer health probes

cards.statement: Standard Load Balancer keeps an established TCP mapping when its backend fails a probe and other backends stay healthy.
cards.explanation: A backend's failed probe changes selection for new flows. Standard Load Balancer leaves existing TCP flows on that backend until connection closure or idle timeout.

source.title: Azure Load Balancer health probes

cards.statement: Standard Load Balancer can map different frontend IPs to the same VM IP and TCP port with Floating IP disabled.
cards.explanation: Enable Floating IP on rules that send traffic from different frontends to the same backend IP and TCP port. Floating IP preserves the frontend address as the packet's destination.
cards.misconception: Different frontend IPs can share the same backend IP and TCP port with Floating IP disabled.

source.title: Multiple frontends for Azure Load Balancer

cards.statement: An inbound NAT rule can distribute traffic for a mapped frontend port among several healthy backend VMs.
cards.explanation: An inbound NAT rule maps a frontend port to a designated backend VM and port. Traffic for that mapping reaches its selected VM rather than being balanced across the pool.
cards.misconception: An inbound NAT rule balances a mapped frontend port's traffic across healthy backend VMs.

source.title: Inbound NAT rules

cards.statement: An administrator can set an internal Standard Load Balancer's frontend to a chosen unused address in its subnet.
cards.explanation: Set the internal frontend's allocation to Static and select an available address from its subnet. This gives clients a stable private destination for the load balancer.

source.title: Azure Load Balancer portal settings

cards.statement: Splitting Azure Storage's Transactions metric by Response type lets an administrator separate success and error trends.
cards.explanation: Splitting the Transactions metric by Response type separates the outcomes into chart series. An administrator can compare successful requests with failures over the same period.

source.title: Analyze metrics with Azure Monitor metrics explorer

cards.statement: Azure Monitor freezes a diagnostic category group's collected categories when an administrator creates the setting.
cards.explanation: When Microsoft changes a diagnostic category group's membership, Azure Monitor updates collection to match. Selecting a group keeps the setting aligned with that group's categories.
cards.misconception: A diagnostic category group captures a fixed list of categories at the time the setting is created.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: A Log Analytics query can combine data from workspaces in different Azure subscriptions.
cards.explanation: A cross-workspace query retrieves data from explicitly referenced workspaces, including those in other subscriptions. The administrator needs query access to the referenced data.

source.title: Query data across Log Analytics workspaces, applications, and resources in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: An alert processing rule can suppress notifications for resources in another Azure subscription.
cards.explanation: An alert processing rule applies to resources within its own subscription. Create a separate rule in another subscription to process that subscription's alerts.
cards.misconception: An alert processing rule's scope extends to resources in other subscriptions.

source.title: Alert processing rules for Azure Monitor alerts

cards.statement: An alert processing rule that adds action groups overrides a matching rule that suppresses action groups.
cards.explanation: A suppression rule takes precedence when addition and suppression rules match the same fired alert. Azure Monitor suppresses the alert's action groups.
cards.misconception: An action-group addition rule wins when it conflicts with a suppression rule.

source.title: Alert processing rules for Azure Monitor alerts

cards.statement: Azure Monitor runs an alert rule's attached action groups in the order the administrator adds them.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor invokes an alert rule's action groups concurrently. Their attachment order does not establish an execution sequence for notifications or automated actions.
cards.misconception: An alert rule's action groups execute sequentially in their attachment order.

source.title: Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: A VM's data collection rule can filter Windows Application events by severity before Azure Monitor Agent sends them.
cards.explanation: In the rule's Windows events data source, choose the Application log and the desired severities. Azure Monitor Agent collects matching events for the associated VM.

source.title: Collect Windows events from virtual machines with Azure Monitor Agent

cards.statement: An administrator saves Storage insights customizations as a separate workbook from the published default.
cards.explanation: Storage insights saves edited metrics and thresholds in an administrator's custom workbook. The published workbook retains its original configuration.

source.title: Monitor Azure Storage services with Azure Monitor Storage insights

cards.statement: Network insights topology includes connected Azure resources across multiple resource groups in the same view.
cards.explanation: Network insights topology represents resource relationships across resource groups. An administrator can follow a network connection beyond a resource group's organizational boundary.

source.title: Network insights

cards.statement: An Access allowed result from IP flow verify confirms the VM's application is listening on the tested port.
cards.explanation: Access allowed describes the security-rule evaluation for the supplied packet. IP flow verify evaluates rules rather than checking whether the application accepts a connection.
cards.misconception: A permitted security-rule result proves that the application is listening on the requested port.

source.title: IP flow verify overview

cards.statement: Connection monitor can use an Azure VM's installed Azure Monitor Agent to run connectivity probes from that source.
cards.explanation: Connection monitor runs Azure VM source checks through the Network Watcher Agent virtual machine extension. Install that extension on an Azure VM used as a monitoring source.
cards.misconception: An Azure VM source uses Azure Monitor Agent to run Connection monitor probes.
tags: Network Watcher Agent virtual machine extension

source.title: Connection monitor overview

cards.statement: Administrators configure Azure Disk Backup in a Recovery Services vault to protect a managed disk.
cards.explanation: Configure Azure Disk Backup in a Backup vault. The managed disk's backup instance and policy belong to that vault.
cards.misconception: Azure Disk Backup uses the same vault type as whole-VM backup.

source.title: Overview of Azure Disk Backup

cards.statement: An administrator can use a Recovery Services vault in one Azure region to back up an Azure VM in another region.
cards.explanation: For Azure VM backup, the Recovery Services vault belongs in the VM's region. Deploy a vault in the workload's region when configuring protection.
cards.misconception: A Recovery Services vault can centrally back up Azure VMs located in other regions.

source.title: Create and configure a Recovery Services vault

cards.statement: Azure Backup freezes a Recovery Services vault's redundancy setting when an administrator configures backup.
cards.explanation: Choose the vault's storage redundancy before enabling VM protection. Azure Backup disables changes to that setting once a backup is configured.

source.title: Create and configure a Recovery Services vault

cards.statement: An administrator can change a protected VM from an Enhanced backup policy to a Standard backup policy.
cards.explanation: Azure Backup prevents changing a protected VM's policy type from Enhanced to Standard. Plan for that restriction when selecting an Enhanced policy.
cards.misconception: A VM protected by an Enhanced policy can return to a Standard policy through a policy change.

source.title: Back up an Azure VM by using the Enhanced policy

cards.statement: An administrator can restore a VM from retained recovery points after stopping its Azure Backup protection.
cards.explanation: Stopping VM protection with backup data retained keeps the existing recovery points available for restore. The VM's scheduled backups stop.

source.title: Manage and monitor Azure VM backups

cards.statement: Azure Backup can remove later-added data disks from a VM's attachments during a Replace existing restore.
cards.explanation: A Replace existing restore applies the disk configuration captured in the recovery point. Data disks attached later fall outside that restored configuration.

source.title: How to restore Azure VM data in Azure portal

cards.statement: An administrator sends vault diagnostic data to Log Analytics to populate Azure Backup reports.
cards.explanation: Azure Backup reports read their reporting data from Log Analytics workspaces. Configure the vault's diagnostic settings to send the relevant data to a workspace.

source.title: Configure Azure Backup reports

cards.statement: By default, Azure Backup generates a built-in Azure Monitor alert when a scheduled VM backup succeeds.
cards.explanation: Azure Backup's built-in job alerts flag failures rather than routine successes. A successful VM backup appears in its job status.
cards.misconception: Azure Backup's built-in alerts include routine notifications for successful scheduled backups.
cards.volatilityNote: The default built-in alert categories for Azure VM backup jobs can change.

source.title: Monitoring and Reporting solutions for Azure Backup

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery requires its cache storage account in the target region for Azure-to-Azure replication.
cards.explanation: The Site Recovery cache storage account belongs in the source region. VM disk changes pass through that cache before Site Recovery sends them to target storage.
cards.misconception: Site Recovery stages replication data in a cache account located in the target region.

source.title: Azure to Azure disaster recovery architecture

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery continues Azure-to-Azure replication while an administrator runs a VM test failover.
cards.explanation: A Site Recovery test failover creates a test VM from replicated data. Production replication continues during the drill.

source.title: Run a test failover (disaster recovery drill) to Azure

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery requires reprotection before an administrator fails a VM back to its primary region.
cards.explanation: After committing failover, reprotect the VM to start replication from the secondary region toward the primary region. Fail back after reprotection completes.

source.title: Reprotect failed over Azure virtual machines to the primary region
